The model builds on the [micromobility toolset](https://github.com/RSGInc/micromobility_toolset){target="_blank"} from RSG, applied to Utah data. It estimates how many bicycle trips happen between small zones and which parts of the bike network they use.

## How it works

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-alt: "Pipeline diagram. Convert the network and create microzones, then run the bike demand model with trip generation, trip distribution and trip assignment, then post-process the outputs."
flowchart LR
  A[Convert<br/>network] --> C[Trip<br/>generation]
  B[Create<br/>microzones] --> C
  C --> D[Trip<br/>distribution] --> E[Trip<br/>assignment] --> F[Post-process<br/>outputs]
```

1. **Convert the network.** Prepares the bike network for the model.
2. **Create microzones.** Builds the small zones the model works in (see below).
3. **Run the bike demand model.** Trip generation, trip distribution and trip assignment.
4. **Post-process outputs.** Produces monthly bike volume across links, microzone-to-microzone trip summaries and microzone centroid nodes, used for quality checks.

## Microzones

Microzones, or micro analysis zones (MAZ), are smaller than the traffic analysis zones used by the [Travel Demand Model](tdm.qmd). They are typically about the size of a census block and group areas with similar land use, such as residential, commercial, industrial, education, parks and open space. They also follow Wasatch Choice Centers, and buildings within a microzone tend to share similar points of access to the network. This finer scale suits bicycle travel, where short trips matter.

## Running the model

The model needs at least 32 GB of RAM and Python 3.

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/rsginc/micromobility_toolset
python Create_Microzones.py        # if microzone data is needed
python Convert_MM_Network.py       # if network data is needed
python utah_bike_demand_model.py   # run the full model
```

Add `--name generate_demand` or `--name assign_demand` to run one step, or `--sample 100` to run only the first 100 microzones. Outputs are saved in the repository's `logs` folder. See the [full instructions](https://github.com/WFRCAnalytics/BDM-Utah-Bike-Demand-Model){target="_blank"}.

## Releases

The Bike Demand Model does not currently publish numbered releases. The repository's latest version is the current model.
